newsitem.title: LEBANON: Judge demands prison for Lebanese labour leader.
newsitem.headline: Judge demands prison for Lebanese labour leader.

text.p: A Lebanese judge issued an indictment on Monday demanding imprisonment of controversial opposition labour leader Elias Abou Rizk for alleged libel, a judicial source said.

The source said investigating judge Said Mirza demanded a sentence of at least six months for Abou Rizk and his supporter Yasser Nehme, secretary general of the opposition wing of the General Labour Confederation (CGTL). Abou Rizk must now appear for trial on the libel charges.

Abou Rizk, 54, was arrested in May after CGTL elections in April produced two leaderships -- one headed by him and one by Ghneim al-Zoghbi, who was recognized by the government. He was held for eight days on charges of falsely claiming to head the CGTL.
Abou Rizk was released in June pending trial in a case that aroused widespread protests in Lebanon.
Mirza's indictment said Abou Rizk and Nehme gave "false news which may defame the Lebanese state's reputation".

The indictment said the two presented a letter to the International Labour Organisation (ILO) in Geneva accusing the Lebanese government of "using all means to control the labour movement through its occupation of the headquarters of the CGTL in south Lebanon and organising a forged election".
An ILO envoy in June criticised Abou Rizk's arrest and demanded his immediate release.

Abou Rizk, who was seeking a second four-year term as CGTL chief, harried Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri during his first term with general strikes and demonstrations to demand better conditions for workers.
His campaign against the government gained wide support from the opposition and he came close to winning election to parliament on a leftwing ticket last summer.
